Jackie2049/perpetual-learning.body:
# perpetual-learning

## Project Overview

A self-evolving intelligence engine that continuously learns, practices, and produces. It learns technical knowledge without interruption, accumulates hands-on experience, identifies directions worth exploring, and produces valuable results. Its domain is AI technology, with priority on Infra. When driven by a user, it prioritizes taking on and refining the user's requirements and ideas. During real operation, it continuously accumulates reusable hands-on experience. The tasks above (tech sourcing, technical secretary work, and experience distillation) are combined so the engine keeps growing stronger, ultimately supporting the user's technical perspective, idea exploration, hands-on experience, and industry influence, and making valuable contributions.

[Open the exploration workbench ↗](https://jackie2049.github.io/perpetual-learning/) · Browse curated results, search knowledge, review logs and pending decisions.

## Operating Mechanism

- **Tech sourcing**: Continuously and autonomously learn, practice, and explore AI technology, prioritizing Infra. Find directions worth going deep on and contributing to, and produce notes, tools, open-source contributions, in-house results, or papers.
- **Technical secretary**: Prioritize taking on the user's needs and vague ideas, and advance goals through due diligence, surveys, value and risk analysis, proofs of concept, and actual execution.
- **Experience distillation**: Accumulate reusable experience from real runs and their feedback, gradually turning it into knowledge, tools, and skills that strengthen future work.

Each piece of work ends with a [log entry](https://github.com/Jackie2049/perpetual-learning/blob/HEAD/diary/readme.md) that records results, failures, and changes in judgment, for later review and reuse. Runtime status and current work are in [WORK.md](https://github.com/Jackie2049/perpetual-learning/blob/HEAD/WORK.md).

### Startup and Control

Start Claude Code in the project directory and give a short instruction:

```bash
claude "开始运行"
```

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `开始运行` (start run) | Automatically reads rules and context, prioritizes user tasks, otherwise autonomously explores AI Infra |
| `继续运行` (continue run) | Resumes the last task and progress |
| `暂停运行` (pause run) | Saves results and next steps, pauses autonomous exploration |
| `查看进展` (view progress) | Reports results, blockers, and next steps |

You can also specify a direction, for example "`开始运行，关注推理优化`" (start run, focus on inference optimization). Work continues within the current session. After the session ends, restart Claude Code and enter "`继续运行`" to pick up where it left off.

## File Organization

This is the single entry point for the whole project. Click a path to browse the file, or click an overview to see the content navigation and usage notes for that section.

| Path | Responsibility | Overview & Index |
|---|---|---|
| [README.md](https://github.com/Jackie2049/perpetual-learning/blob/HEAD/README.md) | Project overview, public presentation, and full navigation | This page |

chenming0v0/OMPiUI.body:
# OMPiUI

**Use the OMP coding assistant on your computer, phone, and browser.**

OMPiUI is a third-party client for [oh-my-pi (OMP)](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi). You can manage coding tasks on your desktop, or connect your phone to a computer or server and continue working on the same project.

The desktop app bundles the interface, the OMPiUI backend, and the official OMP runtime together. The mobile app only provides the interface, and tasks always run on the connected computer or server. There are also two terminal management interfaces: one for managing the headless backend, and one for managing a self-hosted public relay.

[Download](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/releases) · [Server deployment](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/deploy/README.md) · [Self-hosted relay](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/docs/tunnel.md) · [TUI usage guide](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/docs/tui.md)

## What you can do

- **Coding tasks**: chat, view tool execution results, use models and sub-agents, and access OMP's MCP, LSP, and extension capabilities.
- **Continue existing tasks**: share native sessions with the official `omp`. Tasks started in the terminal and in OMPiUI can be opened and continued in either one.
- **Desktop use**: supports Windows, macOS, and Linux. The built-in backend starts automatically when the interface opens, and the title bar shows the local service status.
- **Phone connection**: the Android client supports scanning a QR code or pasting pairing information. The phone browser can also open the address shared by the backend directly.
- **Remote access**: connect to computers on an internal network through a LAN, your own public entry point, or a self-hosted relay.
- **Terminal management**: without a desktop environment, you can check status, start and stop services, adjust network settings, and manage relay tunnels.

## Choose how to use it

| What you want to do | Where to start |
| --- | --- |
| Code on your own computer | Download the desktop installer, configure models and credentials, then use the bundled official OMP |
| Connect your phone to a computer | Install the Android client, or open the address the computer shares in a phone browser |
| Run tasks on a Linux server | Install the backend following the [headless deployment guide](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/deploy/README.md), then connect from your phone or browser |

joylyboy/douyin-live-monitor.body:
# Douyin Live Room Start/Stop Monitor

Automatically monitors a batch of Douyin live rooms. Once a room starts or ends a broadcast, a notification is pushed to iPhone via Bark. Tapping the notification opens Douyin directly through the URL Scheme (`snssdk1128://live`) and enters the corresponding live room.

## How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[External timer / GitHub Actions trigger] --> B[Run monitor.py]
    B --> C[Read rooms.txt]
    C --> D[Request live.douyin.com/room one by one]
    D --> E{Page contains m3u8/flv stream URL?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Mark as live]
    E -- No --> G[Mark as not live]
    F & G --> H[Compare with last state]
    H --> I[Send Bark if state changed]
    I --> J[Tap notification to open Douyin live room]
```

Detection basis: the `liveStatus` field in Douyin's web SSR also returns `normal` for rooms that are live (unreliable). However, on offline room pages, the count of real stream addresses such as `m3u8/flv/pull_url` is 0, while live rooms have many. Therefore, "the page contains real stream addresses" is used as the reliable signal for being live. If the page cannot be fetched or an error occurs, no notification is sent for that check (to prevent false alarms).

## File Overview

- `monitor.py` — Main program: reads rooms.txt, detects live status, sends Bark notifications, and writes state.json.
- `rooms.txt` — Monitoring list. Only this file needs to be edited; monitor.py does not need to be touched.
- `state.json` — Runtime state (last live status), maintained automatically by the program and added to .gitignore.
- `add_room.ps1` — Script for adding rooms from the local command line, independent of this tool (see below).
- `add_room.py` — Python version of the same functionality (backup).
- `.github/workflows/douyin-monitor.yml` — GitHub Actions workflow (native schedule as a fallback).

## rooms.txt Format

One room per line, comma-separated: "link or identifier, display name":

    https://live.douyin.com/125093611494, 子成老师讲家庭教育
    https://v.douyin.com/1_AyxhJoFkc/, 羽川电商

- The display name can be omitted (short links automatically look up the nickname using sec_uid).
- Supported formats:
  - Numeric room ID / Douyin ID (username)
  - `live.douyin.com/room-id`
  - `v.douyin.com/xxxx`…

spincat/SmartProxyPipeline.body:
# SmartProxyPipeline

## Introduction

`SmartProxyPipeline` is an automated proxy subscription processing tool supporting templating, validation, deduplication, consolidation, and upload functionality. It downloads proxy addresses from multiple subscription sources, verifies that these addresses are valid, and uploads the valid addresses to a Git repository. The tool supports two run modes, `local` and `github-action`, and suits scenarios that require proxy addresses to be updated regularly.

## Features

- **Subscription source download**: Generates multiple subscription URLs from the configured subscription source URL templates, and downloads the subscription content concurrently.
- **Address validation**: Uses the `ping` command to verify that downloaded proxy addresses are valid.
- **Git upload**: Saves valid proxy addresses to a file and uploads them to the specified Git repository.
- **Multithreaded processing**: Uses multiple threads to download and validate addresses concurrently, improving processing efficiency.

## Configuration file (`config.json`)

The configuration file defines the program's runtime parameters. The details are as follows:

- **`mode`**: Run mode, either `github-action` or `local`.
- **`download`**: Parameters for downloading subscription sources.
  - `providers`: URL templates for the subscription sources.
  - `retain_days`: Number of days to look back, used to generate subscription URLs.
  - `output_file`: File name in which downloaded addresses are saved.
- **`validation`**: Parameters for validating address validity.
  - `ping_timeout`: Timeout for ping operations.
  - `valid_output_file`: File name in which valid addresses are saved.
  - `validation_interval`: Interval between validations.
- **`proxies`**: Proxy settings.
  - `enable_proxy`: Whether to enable the proxy.
  - `http` and `https`: Proxy addresses.
- **`git`**: Git upload parameters.
  - `enable_git_upload`: Whether to enable Git upload.
  - `repo_url`: URL of the Git repository.
  - `repo_path`: Path of the local Git repository.
  - `username` and `password`: Git username and password (or token).
  - `user_name` and `user_email`: Git user identity information.
